_comment: Every number, label and row shown by a widget on the public site lives here and is editable in Admin → Operational Settings. Anything that asserts a fact about the business stays switched off until it is filled in, so the site never invents figures.

coverage.note: Statuses: high, active, limited, none. States left out are treated as not live. The map does not render at all until enabled.

metrics.note: Results ribbon on Case Studies. Publish only figures you can evidence.

liveFeed.note: Delivery activity panel on the home page. mode: 'simulated' cycles the rows below and is labelled illustrative; 'static' shows them without cycling; 'off' hides the panel.
liveFeed.label: Illustrative delivery activity

board.note: Tiles on the home operations board. Counts marked auto are derived from live content and cannot be faked.

calculator.note: Ranges and defaults for the volume model. It is a model, labelled as such, not a promise.
calculator.disclaimer: An illustrative model using your own inputs. Actual performance depends on vertical, geography and how your team works the calls.

comparison.note: The Web Leads / Inbound Calls / Live Transfers comparison table. Each row is one attribute across the three products.

rows.webLeads: CRM-driven teams with capacity to work records
rows.inboundCalls: Licensed desks that close on the first call
rows.liveTransfers: Small teams that need only qualified conversations

criteria.note: Chips in the qualification builder on sub-vertical and product pages. Sub-vertical criteria are appended automatically.

onboarding.note: Timeline shown on the services index and the contact page.

steps.title: Scoping call
steps.text: We agree vertical, geography, qualification criteria, hours and the volume you can absorb.

steps.title: Program build
steps.text: Campaigns, routing and delivery are configured against your criteria.

steps.title: Delivery test
steps.text: Test calls and records run into your phone system or CRM until the handover is clean.

steps.title: Controlled launch
steps.text: Live at a capped volume so quality can be checked against real outcomes.

steps.title: Scale
steps.text: Caps lift against proven performance, with source-level reporting from the first day.

commercial.note: Pricing model cards. Set recommended to per-call, per-lead, per-transfer or empty for none.

models.name: Per lead
models.how: You pay for each validated record delivered to your CRM in real time.
models.bestFor: Teams with dialling capacity that want volume and control their own follow-up.

models.name: Per call
models.how: You pay for calls that reach your line and pass the agreed billable duration.
models.bestFor: Licensed desks that convert on the first conversation.

models.name: Per transfer
models.how: You pay only for transfers our team has screened against your criteria and warm-handed over.
models.bestFor: Small teams whose agent time is the scarce resource.

glossary.note: Terms defined inline wherever they appear in body copy.

terms.definition: Interactive Voice Response — the automated prompt a caller answers before routing, used to screen for state, product or intent.
The US Telephone Consumer Protection Act. It governs consented contact; every record we deliver carries its consent trail.
A live handover where our agent stays on the line to introduce the consumer to yours, rather than transferring blind.
Answer-Seizure Ratio — the share of routed calls actually answered, the basic health measure of a call program.
The minimum connected time before a call counts commercially, agreed up front and used to settle disputes.

simulated.note: Illustrative activity figures. Each visitor sees the SAME value at the same moment — the number is derived from the clock, not from the visitor — so it drifts through the day without ever showing two people different 'live' data. Always rendered with an illustrative marker.
simulated.label: Illustrative
